citeAs: Xiang Yue, Yuansheng Ni, Kai Zhang, Tianyu Zheng, Ruoqi Liu, Ge Zhang, Samuel Stevens, Dongfu Jiang, Weiming Ren, Yuxuan Sun, Cong Wei, Botao Yu, Ruibin Yuan, Renliang Sun, Ming Yin, Boyuan Zheng, Zhenzhu Yang, Yibo Liu, Wenhao Huang, Huan Sun, Yu Su, Wenhu Chen (2023). MMMU: A Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning Benchmark for Expert AGI. arXiv:2311.16502.
creator: Xiang Yue, Yuansheng Ni, Kai Zhang, Tianyu Zheng, Ruoqi Liu, Ge Zhang, Samuel Stevens, Dongfu Jiang, Weiming Ren, Yuxuan Sun, Cong Wei, Botao Yu, Ruibin Yuan, Renliang Sun, Ming Yin, Boyuan Zheng, Zhenzhu Yang, Yibo Liu, Wenhao Huang, Huan Sun, Yu Su, Wenhu Chen (IN.AI Research, University of Waterloo, The Ohio State University, Carnegie Mellon University, University of Victoria, Princeton University)
description: MMMU (Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning) is a benchmark designed to evaluate multimodal models on massive multi-discipline tasks demanding college-level subject knowledge and deliberate reasoning. It includes 11.5K meticulously collected multimodal questions from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks, covering six core disciplines (Art & Design, Business, Science, Health & Medicine, Humanities & Social Science, and Tech & Engineering) across 30 subjects and 183 subfields, with 30 highly heterogeneous image types.
name: MMMU
rai:annotationsPerItem: Each question was reviewed by at least one secondary reviewer for quality control; human expert evaluation used 3 student experts per subject (each answering 30 questions in their subject area).
rai:annotatorDemographics: Over 50 university students (including co-authors) specializing in the relevant academic majors across 30 subjects. For human expert evaluation, 90 college senior students were selected (3 per subject) to represent experts in the corresponding 30 subjects.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: A secondary review team vetted annotations for quality and guideline adherence. Regular audits of random samples were conducted to ensure sustained quality and consistency. Human expert performance on the validation set ranged from 76.2% (worst) to 88.6% (best), with a median of 82.6%, establishing the human performance ceiling.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Custom web interface developed for data annotation and verification (developed by Tianyu Zheng)
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotators (over 50 university students specializing in relevant majors) collected multimodal questions from free online resources, quizzes, textbooks, and study materials. All questions must contain one or more images, be written in English, and meet college-level difficulty. Annotators categorized each question as multiple-choice or open-ended, and annotated fields including question text, answer options, correct answer, image types, question difficulty, and explanation (if available). Questions were stored in JSON format. Annotators were instructed to avoid data from sources prohibiting copying/redistribution and to select questions without easily accessible answers to mitigate data contamination.
rai:dataBiases: The manual curation process may carry biases. Subjects like law and linguistics were excluded because it was difficult to find enough relevant multimodal problems, potentially limiting coverage. Annotators were advised to select questions without immediately available answers to mitigate data contamination concerns with foundation models. The benchmark focuses on college-level subjects which may not represent all aspects of expert knowledge.
rai:dataCollection: Data was collected in three stages. First, 30 subjects from six disciplines were selected based on the principle that visual inputs are commonly adopted. Second, over 50 university students (including co-authors) specializing in these majors were recruited as annotators to collect multimodal questions from major textbooks, online resources, and lecture materials, creating new questions based on their expertise where necessary. Annotators were instructed to adhere to copyright and license regulations and to select questions without immediately available answers (e.g., answers in separate documents or at the end of textbooks). This resulted in a diverse collection of approximately 13K questions.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Multimodal questions collected from college exams, quizzes, textbooks, online resources, and lecture materials across 30 subjects and 6 disciplines. Questions include images of diverse types such as diagrams, charts, photographs, chemical structures, music sheets, medical images, and more.
rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Document analysis, Web Scraping
rai:dataLimitations: The manual curation process may carry biases. The focus on college-level subjects might not be sufficient for testing Expert AGI as defined. There is no direct mapping between performance on MMMU and "90th percentile of skilled adults," nor are college exams the only tasks an AGI shall tackle. The benchmark is not a sufficient test for Expert AGI on its own.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Two-stage data cleaning: (1) Lexical overlap and source URL similarity were used to identify potential duplicate problems, which were then reviewed by authors to eliminate duplications. (2) Problems were distributed among co-authors for format and typo checking, ensuring adherence to a standardized format. In a third stage, problems were categorized into four difficulty levels (very easy, easy, medium, hard), and approximately 10% classified as very easy were excluded from the benchmark.
rai:dataSocialImpact: MMMU is designed to monitor progress towards Expert AGI, defined as AI reaching at least the 90th percentile of skilled adults in a broad range of tasks. The paper notes that Expert AGI marks a critical milestone that could lead to significant risks of job displacement and economic disruption. The benchmark is intended to stimulate development of next-generation multimodal foundation models and provide a necessary (though not sufficient) test for Expert AGI.
rai:dataUseCases: Evaluating multimodal foundation models on expert-level, college-level multi-discipline understanding and reasoning tasks. Benchmarking progress towards Expert AGI. Assessing LMMs' perception, knowledge, and reasoning capabilities across diverse academic disciplines and image types.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The annotation protocol explicitly states that annotators should avoid collecting questions that contain any private information, and compliance with privacy laws and ethical standards in data handling is paramount.
